first_impression.reaction: I searched 'getting married in costa rica' because James has wanted to go since a uni trip, and it's up against Italy and Mauritius. The intro answers whether it's legal straight away and names the actual office, with no 'pura vida paradise' fluff, so I kept reading. The documents part is properly useful. Then it gets heavy: the Smartraveller crime warnings come before anything that makes me want to go, the Registro Civil route seems to need us both there in person months ahead, and the regions section never names a region. I finished knowing the paperwork order but not whether the notary route is the obvious one for us, or which coast to pick.

journey.quote: Costa Rica is on your shortlist, and before you choose a coast or a resort you want to know one thing: will the marriage stand? It will.
journey.reaction: Straight answer, then the actual legal basis. Dad's first question is handled in the first paragraph.

journey.quote: Many couples sign the civil marriage quietly, then hold the ceremony their guests fly in for wherever they choose.
journey.reaction: Honest trade-off, and it's probably what we'd do. Good to see it said plainly instead of buried.

journey.section: Before you go: entry and documents
journey.quote: Smartraveller rates Costa Rica at level 2, "Exercise a high degree of caution", due to the threat of violent crime, and notes that carjackings and "express kidnappings" are increasingly common.
journey.reaction: I appreciate the honesty, but this is the first thing in the travel section and I'm meant to send this page to my parents. Mum reads 'express kidnappings' and Costa Rica is off the list. It needs to say what that means for a guest group staying at a resort with arranged transfers, not just drop it there.

journey.section: Before you go: entry and documents
journey.quote: Read the full [Smartraveller advice for Costa Rica](https://www.smartraveller.gov.au/destinations/americas/costa-rica) before you book,.
journey.reaction: Stray comma and full stop. Small, but I notice sloppy punctuation on a page asking me to trust it with legal paperwork.

journey.section: The documents you gather at home
journey.quote: That one-month window shapes your timeline more than anything else on the list, so order this certificate last.
journey.reaction: This is the insider detail I want. As a lawyer I'd have missed the one-month validity until it bit us. Copying this into the planning doc.

journey.section: The documents you gather at home
journey.quote: Before you order one, put three questions to the Registro Civil or your notary:
journey.reaction: Good questions, but it's the first of many 'ask them' moments. Fair for a legal page, I just want to know which answers are known and which genuinely aren't.

journey.quote: Because you sign the request together in person, ask the Unidad de Matrimonios how that timing works for applicants who live overseas before you set a date.
journey.reaction: Wait. So for the Registro Civil we both have to turn up in San José to sign, then wait 4 to 6 months? That basically rules it out for us. The page should say so and point us at the notary route as the realistic option, instead of making me work it out.

journey.quote: Choose two people who will be in Costa Rica on the date.
journey.reaction: Obvious once said, but useful. Our best friends will be there anyway.

journey.section: Ceremonies on the beach, in the rainforest or at your resort
journey.quote: If you picture vows on a headland lawn or under a rainforest canopy, the setting rests on your notary, or on a symbolic ceremony after the legal signing.
journey.reaction: At least it answers the beach question rather than dodging it: the office won't come to you, a notary might. Clear enough to act on.

journey.section: Ceremonies on the beach, in the rainforest or at your resort
journey.quote: Strong currents and rip tides occur on the Caribbean and Pacific coasts, lifeguards and warning signs may be absent on public beaches, and crocodile attacks have been reported on the Pacific coast.
journey.reaction: Crocodiles. Fine, useful for the welcome notes. But by now it's warning after warning and nothing about why anyone would choose Costa Rica.

journey.section: When to marry in Costa Rica
journey.quote: Smartraveller places the hurricane and rainy season from June to November, and notes that tropical storms and hurricanes can happen in other months.
journey.reaction: Hurricanes June to November, wet season April to November, Zika. So... December to March? It never actually says which months are good. I came out knowing when not to go.

journey.quote: Choose a region for how guests will reach it.
journey.reaction: Agreed, then it gives me road conditions and malaria in Limón and Puntarenas. No Guanacaste vs Pacific coast vs rainforest comparison, no airport, no drive times. This is the decision we actually face and the section doesn't help.

journey.quote: **Security:** how does your security team work with our private security?
journey.reaction: Our private security? We're a lawyer and a product director, not celebrities. The sole use and drones questions read like they were written for someone else. Makes us feel this isn't for us, and slightly try-hard.

journey.quote: **Deposits and contracts:** whose name is on the contract, in which language is it written, in which currency are payments made, and when do deposits become non-refundable?
journey.reaction: This one is exactly our hidden-costs fear. The colón and US dollar note straight after is useful too.

journey.quote: One Wedded Advisor, start to finish, holds the whole plan together, from venue and travel to vendors and payments.
journey.reaction: 'Start to finish' is what every planner says. Without a Costa Rica wedding or a name on the ground it doesn't land.

journey.section: Plan your Costa Rica wedding with Wedded Concierge
journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor works in your time zone, quotes in AUD, and agrees the fee in writing before any work begins.
journey.reaction: AUD and fee in writing are the right reassurances, calmly put. No hard sell.

Which months are actually good for a wedding with older guests, not just which to avoid?

What does the Smartraveller crime advice mean in practice for a guest group staying at a resort with arranged transfers?
Which Australian document (Single Status or No Record Result) does Costa Rica actually accept?
What do the La Gaceta notice, notary, translations and apostilles roughly cost? (fee amounts deferred)

Do you have a real Costa Rica wedding (venue, region, date) we can look at? (deferred business detail)
How does Wedded Wonderland charge: flat fee, percentage, commissions? Is there a starting range? (deferred business detail)
Will you find the notary, translator and handle the document pack and apostilles, or is that on us? (deferred business detail)
Do you arrange airport transfers in daylight for guests, including grandparents? (deferred business detail)
Are there perks or Wedded Privileges at Costa Rica resorts? (deferred business detail)
How many Costa Rica weddings have you planned? (deferred business detail)

turn_offs_found.quote: **Security:** how does your security team work with our private security?
turn_offs_found.why: Assumes we travel with private security. Pitched at a different, celebrity-type client, which makes the list feel not written for us and a bit showy to share with friends.

turn_offs_found.quote: Smartraveller rates Costa Rica at level 2, "Exercise a high degree of caution", due to the threat of violent crime, and notes that carjackings and "express kidnappings" are increasingly common.
turn_offs_found.why: Honest, but placed first in the travel section with no context for resort-based guests, so it would end the conversation with my parents before they read the useful parts.

turn_offs_found.quote: One Wedded Advisor, start to finish, holds the whole plan together, from venue and travel to vendors and payments.
turn_offs_found.why: Generic end-to-end claim every planner makes; without a Costa Rica wedding or a named person on the ground it reads flatter than the specific advice above it.

would_share_with: James: 'The documents you gather at home' and the witnesses section, because the one-month certificate window and who needs to be there decide our timing

My parents: the intro and the 'Civil, Catholic or symbolic' section only, because Dad will ask if it's legal. I'd hold back the travel section until I've worked out what the crime warning means for us

cta_reaction.quote: When you are ready, [start a conversation with Wedded Concierge](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=getting-married-in-costa-rica&utm_content=closing).
cta_reaction.why: No pressure and the AUD and fee-in-writing lines are right. But we're 14 months out, Costa Rica is one of several options, I don't know which region or months, and I haven't seen a real Costa Rica wedding from them. I'd read the Mauritius guide first.

top_3_changes: Say plainly which legal route suits an overseas couple: 'Because you sign the request together in person, ask the Unidad de Matrimonios how that timing works for applicants who live overseas before you set a date.' leaves us to work out that the Registro Civil may be impractical and the notary route is likely the one.

Give 'Choosing your region' and 'When to marry' something to choose with: name and compare the main wedding regions for airport access and guests, and give a positive steer on months, since 'Choose a region for how guests will reach it.' and the season warnings never say where or when.

Rewrite the resort questions for a couple like us (drop 'our private security' and drone framing) and add one line of context after the Smartraveller crime warning on what it means for resort-based guests with arranged daylight transfers; also fix the stray 'before you book,.'

checks.check: Every journey point and turn-off has an exact quote from the draft

open_questions.question: Does the source pack support stating that the notary route is the practical one for couples living overseas, and how long before the wedding they must be in Costa Rica?
Is there sourced material on wedding regions, airport access or dry-season months that could give 'Choosing your region' and 'When to marry' a positive steer?
Are the private security and drone questions in 'Venues and planning' intended for a different persona? They miss for this couple.

assumptions: Sophie & James arrived via a Google search for 'getting married in costa rica' with Costa Rica on a shortlist, so relevance is 4 and enquiry likelihood is 2 (they enquire after 2 to 3 posts plus a real wedding).

Business details (Wedded Wonderland fees, commissions, on-the-ground team, real weddings, scale proof, perks, Privileges, transfers, paperwork help) and fee amounts are deliberately deferred and not penalised as must-fix.

The 3-minute budget covered the intro, legal, documents, Registro Civil and notary steps, beach, season, region and venue sections and the close in full, with a skim of entry advice, the certificate apostille detail and the FAQ.
